title: A fixed Student t error distribution raised six-month ENSO density score loss at 1981-2024 origins
abstract: We tested whether a fixed Student t error distribution with 5 degrees of freedom improves six-month ENSO probability forecasts. We used NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 Nino 3.4 anomalies and 528 monthly origins in 1981-2024. Both rules shared earlier-only mean forecasts and seasonal variances. Mean negative log density rose from 1.06784 nats for normal errors to 1.09278 for Student errors. The normal-minus-Student gain was -0.02494 nats, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of -0.04845 to -0.00175. Five- and ten-year blocks kept negative limits. Overall 98% interval coverage moved closer to nominal, but its interval-score difference was unresolved. A fixed heavier tail did not improve the full density score in this model. Normal-likelihood variance fitting, revised data, dependent errors and conditional uncertainty limit the result. This does not prove normal ENSO errors or exclude other tail models. The package includes code, source hashes, aggregate results, checks and a figure. External raw records are retrieved separately.

display.caption: Annual density-score gains, conditional three-year block limits, and standardized errors. Positive gains favor Student errors. All error laws have the same forecast means and variances.

citations.reason: Prior seasonal variance benchmark informs the distribution-shape question. The source temperature snapshot overlaps; this is not independent climate evidence.
